As educators put time and care into designing international courses, what do students take away from the experience, and what stays with them after the course ends?

more.title: New Asian flying frog species identified in Indonesia
more.summary: In the lush mountain rainforests of Indonesia, researchers have identified a new species of Asian flying frog with distinctive physical features, calls and unusual egg-laying habits. The discovery is described in a paper published in the journal Zootaxa by scientists from Museum Zoologicum Bogoriense in Indonesia, the University of California, Davis, and other collaborators.

more.title: Optimized supercomputer workflow accelerates protein-structure prediction
more.summary: A Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL)-led team has harnessed the power of El Capitan to accelerate generation of predicted protein structures, drastically reducing the computing time required and opening new possibilities for drug discovery, biological research and national security applications.

more.title: Two proteins key to cellulose synthase trafficking and cell wall formation identified
more.summary: A new study has identified Arabidopsis SNARE proteins VAMP726 and VAMP725 as key components of the trafficking of cellulose synthase (CESA), helping support the formation of both primary and secondary cell walls.

more.title: Repurposed battery molecules drive key chemical reactions where oil meets water
more.summary: The process of producing essential medicines and fine chemicals has long been powered by reactions involving intense heat, heavy-metal catalysts and hazardous hydrogen gas. Now, a team of Harvard chemists and engineers has demonstrated that these critical transformations can be driven cleanly by electricity, right at the boundary where oil and water meet.

more.title: New platform improves accuracy of molecular counting in RNA-sequencing
more.summary: The open-source platform, called UMIche (pronounced "you-me-kay"), is described in a new study published in Nature Communications. It addresses a common challenge in RNA-sequencing, where errors during sequencing can lead to inaccurate measurements of gene expression.

Power plants burned 10% less coal through July of this year, according to a new analysis of federal data from…

more.title: Houston leads large metros in child poverty, disconnected youth
more.summary: Houston is one of the nation's largest economic engines, but for many of its youngest residents, the path to financial stability begins with significant obstacles.

more.title: New model reveals how water moves through tile-drained farm fields
more.summary: Tile drainage fundamentally alters how water moves through agricultural fields, affecting surface ponding, water-table dynamics, crop growth, nutrient transport and water quality. Yet fields with similar drainage systems can respond differently depending on soil, topography and tile design—differences that most models struggle to resolve at the field scale.

more.title: An atlas of vanished places: How climate change is rewriting the books on our shelves
more.summary: On Aug. 26, 2026, a huge mass of rock and ice broke away at an altitude of around 5,200 meters (17,100 feet) in the Himalayas. Within minutes, it became an avalanche of debris and water that hurtled down toward the Nepal-Tibet border, with such force that the seismic signals were initially mistaken for an earthquake.

more.title: Scientists tracked kids for 8 years. What they found about screen time was surprising
more.summary: A surprising Finnish study found that children who spent more time using screens tended to have better cognitive processing abilities as teenagers, challenging the assumption that screen time is always harmful. Researchers suggest that what children do on screens may matter more than how much time they spend using them.

more.title: The hidden language of psychopathy is not what scientists expected
more.summary: Scientists have discovered that psychopathic traits are associated with surprisingly different patterns of language, with some individuals using more positive words and others expressing greater negativity or less anxiety. The findings challenge familiar stereotypes about psychopathy and suggest that the stories people tell about their lives may offer important clues about their personalities.

more.summary: The value of Nvidia’s private investments has nearly tripled over the past nine months, fueled by Jensen Huang’s aggressive dealmaking and rising valuations of its existing portfolio companies.
